Also added BINDER_DOMAIN_INDEX_RETIRED to pipeline.py's HARD_CODES (CompileResult.ok was wrongly True otherwise). Full regression 1518 passed (1511 + 7 new); spec verification 100.00%.
progress_notes.LISS-0424: complete 2026-08-13. Reused the existing Operator-DSL body grammar (OpIndexed/OpBin/OpVar/OpLit, already proven for activity_w[i]*Z[i]-style coefficients) for the classical body instead of inventing new general-expression array-index syntax. Found and fixed during Green: the OpBinder case was initially only added to _bind (covering top-level `Int total = Sigma(...)`), but the real target shape `Sigma(...) == 3` used as a sub-expression crashed with 'cannot evaluate OpBinder as value' since _eval_value is a separate function -- fixed by adding the same dispatch there too. Multi-binding + guard verified to recurse correctly by hand-computing expected marginals, not just checking it runs. Full regression 1523 passed; spec verification 100.00%.
progress_notes.LISS-0425: complete 2026-08-13. -> and => both confirmed already taken (return types/lambdas; match arms) before choosing the Implies keyword. Found during Green: Implies needed wiring into TWO separate grammars, not one -- the general expression grammar AND the Operator-DSL's own _op_expression (Sigma/Pi/future ForAll/Min bodies), which previously had no &&/|| level at all (only the separate where-guard grammar did). Unified by routing _op_expression through a new _op_implies() wrapping the existing _op_guard() chain, rather than maintaining two divergent grammars.
